title.en: Pancreas, adrenal glands, gonads and thymus

text.en: After a sweet snack your blood sugar rises, and your pancreas responds within minutes to bring it back down. Two hormones work like a thermostat for glucose.

The pancreas is both exocrine (pancreatic juice) and endocrine; the islets of Langerhans have alpha cells making glucagon and beta cells making insulin.
Insulin converts glucose to glycogen in the liver and muscles, helps glucose enter cells and lowers blood glucose; glucagon breaks glycogen to glucose and raises it.
Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus with high blood sugar, glucose in urine, frequent urination, thirst and hunger; Banting, Best and MacLeod discovered insulin in 1921.
The adrenal glands lie above the kidneys: the cortex makes cortisol, which is anti-inflammatory and called the life-saving hormone, and aldosterone, which retains sodium and excretes potassium.
The adrenal medulla makes adrenaline and noradrenaline, the flight, fright and fight hormones, which raise heart rate, blood pressure and glucose and dilate the pupils.
The testes (Leydig cells) make testosterone, which controls sperm formation and male secondary sexual characters.
The ovaries make oestrogen from Graafian follicles, for puberty, oogenesis and female characters, and progesterone from the corpus luteum, which maintains pregnancy and prepares the uterus.
The thymus in the upper chest makes thymosin, which stimulates lymphocytes and the immune function.

problem.en: Explain what happens to blood glucose after a meal and after a long fast.

text.en: After a meal glucose rises, so beta cells release insulin.
Glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
After a long fast glucose falls, so alpha cells release glucagon, which turns glycogen into glucose.

prompt.en: List the symptoms of diabetes mellitus and give its cause.

requiredIdeas.en: High blood sugar and sugar in urine

commonMisconceptions.en: Mixing it up with diabetes insipidus (lack of ADH)

points.en: Insulin lowers and glucagon raises blood glucose.
Lack of insulin gives diabetes mellitus.
Adrenal cortex: cortisol and aldosterone; medulla: adrenaline.
Testosterone, oestrogen and progesterone are sex hormones; thymus makes thymosin.
